one_month_reasoning: onsemi's Q3 2026 report is estimated for ~Nov 2, 2026 (unconfirmed; last year's pattern), i.e. just outside the Oct 29 window, so no company earnings print is expected inside it. In-window items: the broad price increase effective Oct 10 (mildly positive, already announced Sep 16), peer analog/power reports in late October (e.g. Texas Instruments, NXP, STMicro) that can move the group either way, and possible S-4/Synaptics shareholder-vote milestones (neutral, largely known). The stock has already bounced ~14% from the $66.60 Analyst Day close (Sep 16), so short-term reversal and momentum roughly offset. With no strong edge I use a near-symmetric lognormal centred slightly below spot (median ~$75.6) with ~17.5% monthly vol (64%/3.5 = 18%, trimmed a touch since no earnings fall in the window).

fair_value.method: Blend of 17x skeptic-haircut NTM EPS of $4.40 (= $75) at 60% weight and a 5% FCF yield on ~$1.7B forward FCF (= $85) at 40% weight, giving ~$79.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS as of Sep 2027 $4.40 x 17x forward P/E

inputs_detail.derivation: Haircut FY27 consensus ~10% to ~$4.10 for cyclical auto exposure, Chinese SiC pricing pressure and power-discrete pricing risk flagged by TD Cowen, then roll forward ~9 months with ~10% growth; Synaptics (close mid-2027, 12% dilution, accretive only within 18 months) treated as roughly EPS-neutral in the window.
Current forward P/E is near 17x per Sep 17 coverage; I hold it flat rather than re-rate, since the bull re-rating needs AI-DC and 2030 targets that land mostly in 2028+ (Analyst Day critique).

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: Forward FCF ~$1.7B / 5% yield = $34B equity, less ~$0.6B net debt, / 397M diluted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus $7.42B haircut ~5% for cycle risk and business exits weighing on growth.
Cyclical auto/industrial semi with ~8% short float and China SiC competition warrants a yield above large-cap analog peers; 5% sits between trough (6-7%) and peak (3-4%) cycle valuations.

bear.story: Auto/industrial recovery stalls (Europe auto weak), Chinese SiC substrates (~$400 vs ~$1,200/wafer) crush SiC pricing, power-discrete pricing fades once the Oct 2026 hikes lap, AI-DC content disappoints; FY27 EPS ~$3.2 and multiple compresses to ~14x, with Synaptics dilution and integration noise from mid-2027. Revisits the 52-week low area.

base.story: Margins keep recovering toward 41-42% gross, FY27 EPS lands ~$4.1-4.5, AI-DC grows but the 2030 roadmap is not paid for in advance; Synaptics closes mid-2027 roughly EPS-neutral; multiple holds ~17x.

bull.story: Tight supply (lead times 27->32 weeks, broad price increases) plus 800V DC AI rack content drive upside revisions; FY28 EPS path >$5.2 and the market re-rates toward 22-23x, retracing toward the June high.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$50 (about 11x FY27 consensus and ~34% below spot, near the Mar-Apr 2026 trading range) the price would most likely reflect a genuine earnings reset: Q3/Q4 guide-downs from auto/industrial demand, SiC price collapse from Chinese competition, or a failed/renegotiated Synaptics deal, rather than ordinary volatility in a 64%-vol stock.

Durability of pricing power in power discretes and SiC against subsidised Chinese substrate/device makers

Semiconductor-sector beta and macro risk in a 64%-realised-vol stock
reasoning: Skeptic lane. Facts: Q2 2026 revenue $1.60B (+9% y/y), non-GAAP EPS $0.74, TTM FCF margin 24.2%, net debt ~$0.6B, 397M diluted shares; Q3 guide $1.65-1.75B / EPS $0.81-0.93. Consensus FY26/FY27 EPS $3.20/$4.53, revised up over 60-90 days, so at $75.95 the stock trades ~17x FY27, not demanding. The bear evidence is real but mostly about timing and quality rather than solvency: the stock halved from the $134.92 June peak after the all-stock ~$7B Synaptics deal (Jun 25, ~12% dilution, close mid-2027) and a TD Cowen downgrade citing narrative dilution, niche NPU assets, thin revenue synergies, elevated inventory, business exits and power-discrete pricing pressure; the Sep 16 Analyst Day (2030: $11B revenue, 53% GM) fell 9% because payoff is 2028+ and the TAM slide shrank $30B; Chinese SiC wafers at ~1/3 the Western cost forced Czech job cuts; the CFO sold 90k shares in April at $80-100; short float ~8% (June). Offsetting: balance sheet is strong (0.6x pro forma net leverage, convertibles, no covenant stress found), estimates are rising, lead times are extending and a broad price increase takes effect Oct 10. So I find no hidden accounting or credit landmine; the downside is a cyclical earnings miss plus multiple compression. Fair value ~$79 (P/E $75 at 60%, FCF yield $85 at 40%). Scenarios 25/50/25 at $45/$80/$120 give a mean ~$81 and median ~$77. Ladder: lognormal around a ~$76-77 median with ~52% vol (below the 64% realised, which was inflated by the rally-and-crash) and a fattened left tail to reflect the 25% bear case. Research was limited: onsemi IR pages returned 503 and paid data endpoints (price targets, statistics) were unavailable; no credit-agency reports were reachable.
